threads.body:
@copilot Update this PR directly to simplify its new Thrift and AWS Lambda SQS factory tests while preserving meaningful coverage of explicit schema selection. Do not create a separate follow-up PR or change the PR's base branch.

Remove instrumentation/aws-lambda/aws-lambda-events-common-2.2/library/src/test/java/io/opentelemetry/instrumentation/awslambdaevents/common/v2_2/internal/AwsLambdaSqsInstrumenterFactoryTest.java after moving its useful scope-schema assertions into existing SQS integration tests. Assert https://opentelemetry.io/schemas/1.43.0 on both batch and per-message processing spans and their emitted metrics. Existing coverage includes AwsLambdaSqsMessageHandlerTest.processSpans, keyedEventSuppressesSelectedMessage, and AwsLambdaSqsNestedEventHandlerTest.distinctNestedEventStartsProcessing under instrumentation/aws-lambda/aws-lambda-events-3.11/library/src/test/java/io/opentelemetry/instrumentation/awslambdaevents/v3_11/, plus AwsLambdaSqsMetricsAssertions under instrumentation/aws-lambda/aws-lambda-events-2.2/testing/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/instrumentation/awslambdaevents/v2_2/. Reuse those tests and metric assertions instead of adding another suppression or processing test suite.

Narrow instrumentation/thrift-0.13/library/src/test/java/io/opentelemetry/instrumentation/thrift/v0_13/internal/ThriftInstrumenterFactoryTest.java to a small factory-specific regression proving that client and server span/metric schema selection follows the passed OpenTelemetry instance rather than global RPC configuration. Preserve the useful same-process per-instance distinction that the existing separate-JVM integration variants cannot detect. The expected schema is https://opentelemetry.io/schemas/1.37.0 for legacy RPC and https://opentelemetry.io/schemas/1.44.0 for preview RPC. Remove the duplicated generic RPC attribute and metric-name matrix already covered centrally by RpcInstanceSemconvTest. Its current assertion of "custom Service/method" is identical in every mode and does not establish mode-specific initialization of the wrapped name extractor; do not retain that assertion as purported per-instance naming coverage.

Keep production behavior and the explicit schema selections unchanged. Do not remove schema coverage without its replacement, expand this into a broader schema audit, or duplicate shared-helper coverage. Follow the repository instructions, use existing assertion helpers where appropriate, and validate the affected tests with the narrowest relevant formatting and test commands.

replies.body: Addressed in 5fe07a35. SQS schema assertions now use the existing processing and metrics tests, and the Thrift factory test now verifies per-instance span and metric schemas for both client and server instrumenters.

Addressed in 6d8ab139. The factory test is removed, and the existing Thrift integration assertions now verify span and metric schema URLs across legacy, preview, and dual-emission modes for both library and javaagent variants.

@copilot Update this PR directly with a test-only cleanup of the four new JDBC scope-schema assertions. Do not create a follow-up PR as a workaround.

In instrumentation/jdbc/library/src/test/java/io/opentelemetry/instrumentation/jdbc/datasource/JdbcTelemetryTest.java, replace the four hand-written satisfies lambdas that assert getInstrumentationScopeInfo().getSchemaUrl() equals "https://opentelemetry.io/schemas/1.44.0" with satisfies(hasScopeSchemaUrl(SchemaUrls.V1_44_0)). There are two span expectations and two metric expectations. Add a static import of io.opentelemetry.instrumentation.testing.util.InstrumentationScopeAssertions.hasScopeSchemaUrl and import io.opentelemetry.semconv.SchemaUrls as needed.

This consolidates the previously requested JDBC shared-helper cleanup with the matching version-constant cleanup. Use the version-specific SchemaUrls.V1_44_0 constant for the expected value, not the production DbSchemaUrls.SCHEMA_URL alias, so a production schema-version change cannot silently change the expectation too.

Acceptance criteria: all four JDBC schema assertions use the shared helper and the version-specific constant, with unchanged expected values and all other assertions and coverage preserved. Keep changes scoped to JdbcTelemetryTest.java. Preserve all production changes, the existing Thrift and SQS cleanup, the current base branch and draft/ready state, and do not update other PR branches, restack, merge, post replies, or resolve threads. Follow repository formatting and targeted validation instructions.
